chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who fasted in the month of Ramadan, so he ate and drank out of forgetfulness. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let him complete his fast, and there is no making up for it upon him.'
ai.seo_question: Does eating or drinking out of forgetfulness break the Ramadan fast?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that forgetfulness (nasi) is a valid excuse for breaking the fast, rendering the day complete without requiring a makeup (qada) day. This ruling is derived from the principle that Allah does not hold individuals accountable for unintentional errors, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of acts performed in a state of unawareness.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who Fasts in the Month of Ramazan, so he eats and drinks out of forgetfulness. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Let him complete his Fast, and there is not making up for it upon him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah, who has said the following: “I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who because of forgetfulness when fasting in the month of Ramadan eats and drinks. He (the Imam) said, ‘He is not required to complete its Qada’ (compensatory fast).
